agent.title: About me
paragraphs: I'm Alba Rodríguez. I trained in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at The Bridge and I'm now specialising in generative AI and agents.
I build projects around real use cases: agents that use tools, RAG over business documents, databases and interfaces you can try. And I document what didn't work and what's still left.
I use AI tools (Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT) to speed up development and debugging — AI doesn't replace judgement, it amplifies it.
I'm looking for my first role as a Junior AI Engineer in a team where I can keep learning and contribute from day one.

state.title: Education and path
state.intro: Each stage of my training is a new message appended to state["messages"], starting with Marketing and Advertising.

bootcamp.name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Bootcamp — The Bridge
bootcamp.desc: Intensive project-based training with Python, Machine Learning and production deployment.

messages.title: Data Analysis
messages.desc: Data access (files, APIs, web scraping), SQL databases and an introduction to NoSQL, cleaning and preprocessing, EDA, feature engineering and advanced visualisation.

messages.title: Machine Learning
messages.desc: Supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation, cross-validation, neural networks (DNN, CNN, RNN), transfer learning, fine-tuning and an introduction to generative AI.

messages.title: Data Science & Business
messages.desc: Productising and deploying models, storytelling and communicating results, building business-oriented data products.

messages.title: Generative AI and Agents
messages.desc: Self-taught training, separate from the bootcamp, in LLMs, RAG, prompt engineering and agent development with LangChain and LangGraph, applied in my own projects.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.desc: Native spoken and written communication. Technical writing, presentations and documentation.

languages.name: English
languages.desc: Solid reading and listening: fluent reading of technical documentation, papers and specialised resources. Functional speaking, able to hold professional conversations with growing confidence.

now: Building a lead generation platform with agents: right now, a multi-agent system that audits websites.
Going deeper into RAG, LLM evaluation and engineering best practices.

tools.title: Agent projects
tools.intro: Each project is a tool the agent can call. Hover, focus with the keyboard or press “Show the call” to expand the arguments and the run.
tools.note: Function signatures are an illustrative representation; the nodes, tools and figures are the real ones from each project.

main.title: Lead qualification agent
main.desc: A LangGraph graph built node by node: it researches a company's website, copies the evidence word for word and turns it into structured data with Pydantic. The final decision is made by tested business rules, not the LLM. Evaluated in LangSmith on 35 real leads checked against each company's website: analysing the failures took it from 90% to 99%.

main.title: AI booking assistant
main.desc: An agent with 11 tools that books, changes and cancels appointments for a hair salon on SQLite with atomic transactions. It answers business questions with RAG (Chroma), mirrors the schedule to Google Calendar and ships three Streamlit apps: customer chat, staff schedule and owner dashboard.

tools.secondaryTitle: Secondary tools · Data Science and APIs

secondary.title: Traffic Violations API
secondary.desc: REST API with FastAPI serving a machine learning model that predicts traffic violations. Deployed on Render and publicly available.

secondary.title: Traffic Violations ML
secondary.desc: Classification model that predicts traffic violations from historical data, applying classification and model evaluation techniques.

secondary.title: Airbnb price analysis
secondary.desc: Exploratory analysis of Airbnb data in Madrid: neighbourhood and room type are the factors that best explain price variation.

retriever.title: Stack
retriever.intro: The tools I work with, indexed by category.

guardrails.title: How I build reliable agents
guardrails.intro: Two rules that sum up how I make the LLM useful without trusting it blindly. Your message has to pass both.

rules.title: AI extracts, code decides
rules.desc: The LLM understands the text and copies the evidence word for word. Scoring, limits (tool_choice="none"), the identified customer and dates are set by code, with tests.

rules.title: Measure before improving
rules.desc: A LangSmith dataset of 35 real leads with 5 evaluators: going through every failure in the traces took it from 90% to 99%. And consistent data: atomic SQLite bookings.

evaluator.title: How I work
evaluator.intro: My process, shown as an evaluation pipeline: every step leaves a trace you can review.

steps.title: Use case
steps.desc: Understand the business need and what the assistant or agent has to solve.

steps.title: Agent design
steps.desc: Choose tools, information sources (RAG), memory, and how it connects to APIs and databases.

steps.title: Testing and evaluation
steps.desc: Automated tests for the deterministic logic and LangSmith datasets and traces to measure the agent's answers.

steps.title: Interface and deployment
steps.desc: Streamlit interfaces and FastAPI APIs, deployed to the cloud.

steps.title: Documentation
steps.desc: READMEs with the technical decisions and known limitations, so the project can be understood and improved.
